articles.title: El Manchester City, culpable de infringir las normas financieras de la Premier
articles.standfirst: Aún no se ha anunciado oficialmente ninguna sanción y se espera que el club apele la decisión
articles.summary: Aún no se ha anunciado oficialmente ninguna sanción y se espera que el club apele la decisión
articles.body: El Manchester City, según adelantó The Athletic y anunciaron, posteriormente, los principales medios de Inglaterra, ha sido declarado culpable en prácticamente todas las acusaciones (en 114 de 115) relacionadas con infracciones de las regulaciones financieras de la Premier League. Aún no se ha anunciado oficialmente ninguna sanción y se espera que el City apele la decisión. Aunque el club ha negado estas acusaciones reiteradamente, la Comisión Independiente que estudia el caso ha fallado y, de acuerdo con estas informaciones, lo ha considerado culpable en casi todos los casos en que había sospechas. La Premier League acusó en febrero de 2023 al City de no proporcionar información financiera precisa ni los detalles correctos de pagos a entrenadores y jugadores entre las temporadas 2009-2010 y 2017-2018, de no cumplir con el 'fair play' financiero de la UEFA entre 2009 y 2018 y con el de la Premier League entre la 2015-2016 y la 2017-2018, así como de no cooperar con las investigaciones de la Premier que tuvieron lugar entre diciembre de 2018 y febrero de 2023. "El proceso de la Premier League sigue en curso, con importantes detalles por completar, y está sujeto a estricta confidencialidad. Por lo tanto, la postura del Manchester City FC se mantiene coherente con la declaración del club de febrero de 2023", ha asegurado, tras conocer las informaciones de esta tarde, un portavoz del City, según recoge The Telegraph. “Durante ocho años, el club ha respetado diligentemente el debido proceso, partiendo de la base de que la junta directiva y el comité ejecutivo de la Premier League se comportarían como un organismo regulador independiente, imparcial y justo, libre de influencias partidistas", continúa el portavoz. El City ha negado desde el inicio todos los cargos de los que se le acusa y contrató a algunos de los mejores abogados especializados en deporte en el Reino Unido para tratar de limpiar su nombre y evitar una sanción, que aún no se conoce y que podría ir desde una multa económica hasta la deducción de puntos, descenso de categoría e incluso pérdida de títulos. Pero eso está por ver.

articles.title: Mensaje de Eto'o a Lamine Yamal en la lucha por el Balón de Oro
articles.standfirst: El exazulgrana se deshace en elogios hacia el extremo de Rocafonda
articles.summary: El exazulgrana se deshace en elogios hacia el extremo de Rocafonda
articles.body: La votación para elegir al próximo ganador del Balón de Oro encara ya su recta final. El lunes se cerrará el plazo y, en las últimas horas, son muchos los jugadores, exjugadores y profesionales vinculados al mundo del fútbol que están haciendo públicas sus opiniones sobre los principales candidatos al prestigioso galardón. Uno de los últimos en pronunciarse ha sido Samuel Eto'o. El exdelantero camerunés ha recurrido a sus redes sociales para mostrar públicamente su apoyo a Lamine Yamal y dedicarle un mensaje directo antes de que se cierre el plazo de la votación. Eto'o ha compartido en su cuenta de Instagram una fotografía del joven futbolista acompañada de unas palabras. "Balón de Oro de nuestros corazones. ❤️🏆 Genio, audaz, talentoso… Mucha suerte en esta carrera por el Balón de Oro. Pero, sea cual sea el veredicto, hay algo que ya es seguro: al igual que Ousmane, tú ya eres el Balón de Oro de nuestros corazones. Sigue haciéndonos soñar", ha escrito el camerunés. Con este mensaje, el exjugador quiso poner en valor el talento y la trayectoria de Lamine Yamal, independientemente de cuál sea el resultado final. Eto'o acompañó su publicación con una imagen de Lamine Yamal durante un encuentro. Ahora, habrá que esperar al anuncio oficial, el próximo 26 de octubre, para conocer quién se lleva finalmente el Balón de Oro. Hasta entonces, el debate y los mensajes de apoyo continuarán protagonizando la actualidad futbolística.

articles.title: Rangers: 100 days of Derek McInnes at Ibrox
articles.summary: BBC Scotland charts the first tumultuous 100 days of Derek McInnes' tenure as Rangers manager.
articles.body:
Derek McInnes has been in charge for 100 days at Rangers - the club he grew up supporting, played for and previously turned down the opportunity to manage.

In his brief but busy tenure, there has been a huge squad overhaul, while a sluggish start led to Ibrox jeers and the failure to qualify for European football for the first time in a decade.

Then came September. A golden start to autumn quietened talk of crisis as a winning streak extended to six games, including two Old Firm derby victories.

BBC Sport Scotland charts the key moments of McInnes' reign.

Penrice focuses on Rangers as Scotland remains a target

How derby masterclasses provide stark Rangers contrast

17 June - A new beginning - 'Lot of hard work ahead'

One month and one day after his Heart of Midlothian side were pipped to the title by Celtic on the final day of last season, McInnes is announced as Rangers manager, replacing the departed Danny Rohl.

It is 26 years since his days as a Rangers player ended with a move to West Bromwich Albion and eight-and-a-half years since he turned down the chance to become boss under the chairmanship of Dave King.

"It is no secret that I grew up a Rangers supporter and I am convinced this is the right time to take on this prestigious role," McInnes says. "There is a lot of hard work ahead."

31 July - First night nerves & 'Not good enough to win'

The new era begins at Tannadice with a whimper rather than a bang as Thelo Aasgaard scores a second-half equaliser in a 1-1 draw with Dundee United.

"We worked hard to get back into it, but I don't think we were good enough to win the game," McInnes says. "I thought the point was the right scoreline and we're disappointed with that first half.

"We wasted a lot, we didn't create too much and it was a bit too frantic."

6 August - European debut & 'We beat ourselves'

Curtain up on Rangers European campaign - and it does not start well.

A trip to eastern Poland in the first leg of their Europa League third qualifying round tie ends in a 2-1 defeat by Jagellonia Bialystok.

McInnes notes: "I just felt we beat ourselves, to be honest. We got off to a good start, being patient with what we were trying to do. We made two mistakes for the two goals."

Rangers' first home match of the season ends also ends in a 2-1 defeat, this time by Hibernian.

A late Callum Wright goal seals victory for the Edinburgh side and, to make matters worse, striker Youseff Chermitti suffers an ACL injury that scuppers any potential big-money sale amid reports of interest from Galatasaray.

"There are little things going against us at the minute, but we have to stay strong - we're not as bad as people think," McInnes insists. "At the minute, we are trying to work boys back to the same level of fitness and trying to manage that situation.

"I understand the fan frustration. They want and expect to see their team win. I share the frustration."

Another below-par performance has supporters up in arms.

Shankland scores from the penalty spot, but a second-half goal from Nik Prelec earns Jagellonia a draw on the night and progress on aggregate.

McInnes confesses: "It is not great to watch. My team go from some good highs in the first half to being as poor as we were in the second half and you have to say we didn't do enough. We should be winning this game."

Five games into the new season and Rangers record their first win under McInnes - an emphatic 5-1 thumping of holders St Mirren in the Premier Sports Cup.

"We gave up a couple of chances, which we weren't too pleased about, but there was a good attacking threat from the team," McInnes concludes.

"The players deserved that moment today against a St Mirren team who have been doing well."

26 August - 'Embarrassing' European exit

A penalty shoot-out defeat by the unfancied Czechs eliminates Rangers from Europe altogether.

Missed spot kicks by Findlay Curtis and James Penrice hand victory to Jablonec after a 1-0 defeat. A bitter blow for the balance sheet too as the Ibrox club face up to life without European football proper for the first time in 10 years.

"I'm embarrassed with the performance," McInnes says. "I think the only people who represented the club well tonight were my support staff and the supporters who, to a man, were outstanding, getting behind the team despite watching what we all watched."

McInnes registers his first Scottish Premiership win as Rangers manager at his old stamping ground of Pittodrie.

A Shankland penalty gets the job done, much to McInnes' relief as he praises Kim Min-Su as evidence that the summer recruitment is beginning to bear fruit.

"It was a tough few days for us all," he says. "I thought we were far more like the Rangers team I want us to be."

5 September - 'We'd have taken any sort of win'

After a 2-1 success at Falkirk, a third successive Premiership win, but it comes at a cost as Shankland tears a hamstring against Motherwell at Ibrox and will be sidelined for months. Ryan Nederi replaces the captain and scores the only goal.

"We'd have taken any sort of win because we're up against a good team, but I really enjoyed how many chances we created," McInnes says.

9 September - Beating Buddies again, with last-gasp goal

It looks like Rangers' winning run is coming to an end until Bojan Miovski comes off the bench to score a stoppage-time winner at home to St Mirren to spark wild celebrations.

Rangers move into second place in the Premiership, five points behind leaders Celtic.

With four wins on the bounce, McInnes is sounding more optimistic.

"There are obviously loads we have to improve on, but we have to keep winning while we are looking for those improvements," he says.

McInnes demanded a big performance from his players in his Old Firm managerial debut - and he got it.

He pulled a few tactical surprises and they paid off as Rangers power into the Premier Sports Cup semi-finals.

Two goals from the inspired Dan Neill and a first for Kelsy set up a meeting with Aberdeen at Hampden.

"It was the performance and result we were all looking for," McInnes says. "It's a good reference point for my players. They're a young squad and they saw how much that result means to the supporters."

Glasgow's big two meet again, this time at Celtic Park in the Premiership.

A Naderi goal stuns the 60,000 home supporters and moves Rangers two points behind their Glasgow rivals.

Afterwards, McInnes reflects: "It's just three points and it gets us three points closer to Celtic. We understood if we lost the game, that distance just starts to feel uncomfortable for us.

"I like putting my name to this team at the minute and I think we've got a good thing going."

Analysis: Rangers finding togetherness and ways to win

Former Rangers interim boss and Captain Barry Ferguson

"I've been really impressed since exiting in Europe.

"I think the reaction, not just the manager and the coaching staff, the players, I've been very impressed. Even before the two Celtic games, they played well in parts of it, other parts they didn't, but they found a way to win, and that's so important.

"It's always going to take a bit of time because there was a big turnaround of players and some players hit the ground running.

"It takes some players a wee bit of time to get going. But now I think you're starting to see a team that's got a real togetherness. That's the biggest thing for me."

articles.title: El Carlos Tartiere, territorio prohibido para el Sporting
articles.standfirst: El equipo rojiblanco no gana un derbi en el estadio del Real Oviedo desde octubre de 2001 y acumula nueve visitas consecutivas sin lograr la victoria
articles.summary: El conjunto rojiblanco no gana un derbi en el estadio del Real Oviedo desde octubre de 2001 y acumula nueve visitas consecutivas sin conseguir la victoria
articles.body: El Sporting afrontará este domingo uno de los grandes retos que todavía se le resisten en el derbi asturiano. El conjunto rojiblanco lleva casi 25 años sin ganar al Real Oviedo en el Carlos Tartiere. La última vez ocurrió el 28 de octubre de 2001, cuando se impuso por 0-2 gracias a los goles de Lozano y David Villa. Desde entonces, nueve visitas del Sporting al feudo azul y ninguna victoria. La racha comenzó la temporada siguiente, cuando el Oviedo ganó 2-1, antes de que los caminos de ambos primeros equipos se separasen durante más de una década. El derbi regresó al Tartiere en la 2017/18 y desde entonces el dominio local se ha mantenido. El balance global desde aquella derrota de 2001 es de cinco victorias del Oviedo y cuatro empates, incluidos los dos últimos precedentes, que terminaron 0-0 en la 2023/24 y 1-1 en la 2024/25. El dato añade un ingrediente más a un derbi al que los dos equipos llegan con cuentas pendientes. El Oviedo, que encadena cinco enfrentamientos sin derrotar al Sporting, tratará de acabar con su propia sequía. Los rojiblancos, mientras, buscarán hacer lo mismo con una espera mucho más larga en territorio enemigo. Casi un cuarto de siglo después, el Tartiere vuelve a poner a prueba una de las grandes rachas del derbi asturiano.

articles.standfirst: El mediocentro madrileño sigue muy enfadado por el gol que le anularon ante el Getafe
articles.summary: El mediocentro madrileño sigue muy enfadado por el gol que le anularon ante el Getafe
articles.body: Carlos Dotor vive su segundo año en Málaga. El mediocentro madrileño se convirtió en un pilar clave del ascenso y en uno de los futbolistas que más juego dio en las celebraciones del ascenso. Ahora, con el equipo en Primera, atiende a MARCA para hablar del aterrizaje de los blanquiazules en la máxima categoría. Lo hace una semana después de anotar su primer gol en la élite y muy enfadado con el tanto anulado en el Coliseum ante el Getafe. Pregunta. El inicio en Primera está siendo duro. ¿Cómo lo está viviendo el vestuario? R. El inicio está siendo difícil, pero podía pasar. Hemos dado un salto de calidad y, a veces, es complicada esa adaptación a la categoría. Terminamos muy tarde y había mucha euforia en la ciudad; te crees que eres una estrella del rock. Ahora nos han puesto en nuestro sitio. Estamos asimilando dónde estamos; hemos hecho tramos de partido buenos. Estamos con confianza, aunque entran ciertas dudas. P. ¿Falta adaptación a la categoría y de ahí estos resultados? R. Seguramente haya un punto en el que necesitamos una adaptación a la categoría. Somos pocos los que hemos jugado en Primera; es un ritmo al que hay que acostumbrarse. Hemos hecho ciertos partidos, sobre todo contra los rivales de nuestro nivel, pero nos falta coger esas dinámicas que caigan hacia nuestro lado. El año pasado se nos atragantaban partidos al principio, pero cogimos la dinámica y fue saliendo de cara. P. ¿Qué piensas que le falta al equipo para ganar? R. A veces tienes la sensación de que dominas el partido, pero igual el otro equipo piensa lo mismo. Hay que ser más consciente de que hay que estar con los cinco sentidos puestos. En cualquier jugada te pueden hacer gol. P. ¿Cómo está el ambiente dentro del vestuario? R. Estamos bien. Tampoco puede ser esto un funeral, queda mucho y tenemos mucho que decir. Tenemos que estar juntos, aunque lógicamente se van a hablar muchas cosas. La gente va a hablar, pero tenemos que estar juntos y centrarnos en crear un ambiente sano. P. ¿Qué les transmite Funes ante esta situación? R. Nos dice que tranquilidad. Todos los días va a salir el sol. Si nos empezamos a poner nerviosos y a hacer la guerra por nuestra cuenta, no va a salir nada. Vamos a ser positivos y a recuperarnos bien en todos los aspectos. Si todos arrimamos el hombro, todo va a sumar. P. ¿Tenías claro que querías volver al Málaga? R. Quería volver y el Málaga quería que volviera. El Celta no puso las cosas muy complicadas, pero al principio hubo algo de duda. No me quería hacer ilusiones porque nunca se sabe. Hubo conversaciones y fue despedida sabiendo que se podía dar que volviera. El club me transmitió que quería que volviese y fuimos hablando durante el verano. Se cerró rápido. Los clubes son empresas y me compraron hace unos años; es una inversión que hicieron. Intento jugar donde quiero, pero hay que entender a los clubes. Son dos partes y hay que escuchar las dos versiones. P. ¿Te ha sorprendido el nivel de algunos equipos de Primera? R. Hablé con mis amigos de que el Madrid y el Atleti ya te esperabas que fueran aviones, pero el Villarreal también. Es un equipo de Champions. P. ¿Qué te pareció lo ocurrido con el gol anulado en Getafe? R. El árbitro me dijo que era muy justo y que lo estaban revisando. Me parece de vergüenza que me digan que no funciona la herramienta que has comprado; es una feria. Es triste que pase en la Primera División de España. Que me digas que no te funciona es penoso. Me parece drástico que te corten un gol por un fuera de juego milimétrico; además, si después se inventan un fuera de juego con escuadra y cartabón. Me parece que no es de una liga seria lo de que no funcione la herramienta. Que falle eso me parece de no ser serio. Era un gol en el añadido de la primera parte. Era un gol psicológico, pero ya está. P. ¿Debe cambiar la idea de juego del Málaga en Primera? R. En el área pasan cosas y hay que poner el balón ahí. La identidad tiene que ser la misma. Tenemos que ser conscientes de que nos falta gente y de que han sido y van a ser importantes. Eso también juega a nuestro favor. Tenemos que dar un paso más en la toma de decisiones y que sea más rápida. Esas cosas las vamos a ir cogiendo. Una vez has llegado a tres cuartos, hay que hacer rupturas y que pasen cosas, tener el objetivo de hacer gol. P. ¿Se ha hablado en el vestuario de la posible llegada de algún fichaje? R. No se ha comentado nada. Mis amigos me comentaron lo de Martial y lo de Zaha, pero no te puedo decir nada. No sé ni dónde juegan. Si están bien y el club lo ve bien, que vengan. Si no, pues no. Cuando te dicen los nombres te sorprende, pero la situación actual es otra cosa. P. Si pudieras pedir un fichaje, ¿qué perfil elegirías? R. Algo con experiencia nos podría venir bien, pero con lo que tenemos nos va a dar. Esa experiencia la podemos coger nosotros, pero igual es importante que venga uno que sepa de qué va esto. Me gustó mucho Gueye ante el Villarreal, me gustó mucho ese equipo. A lo mejor crees que son jugadores más terrenales, pero después flipas.

articles.title: Manchester City charges: Premier League club found guilty of breaking majority of 115 financial rules
articles.summary: Manchester City are found guilty of breaking the majority of the 115 financial rules they were accused of breaching, sources tell BBC Sport.
articles.body:
Manchester City have been found guilty of breaking the majority of the 115 financial rules they were accused of breaching, sources have told BBC Sport.

The Athletic , external is reporting that the sanctions have not been decided but that the independent panel has reached its decision, finding the club guilty of all but one count.

Sources have also told BBC Sport a decision has been made in the case, and City have been found guilty of the majority of breaches.

Asked if the report was correct, City did not comment either way.

Instead they released a statement saying the "Premier League process remains ongoing with significant elements to be completed, and subject to strict confidentiality".

"The club has diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis that the Premier League board and executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair-minded regulator, free from partisan influence," it added.

BBC Sport has also been told that, in the event of being found guilty, City will appeal against the findings.

Other Premier League clubs are believed to have been informed about the independent panel's decision.

Man City and the 115 charges - key questions answered

In February 2023, City were charged with more than 100 breaches of the Premier League's financial rules following a four-year investigation.

The club was referred to an independent commission over allegations it breached financial rules between 2009 and 2018.

The hearing began in September 2024 behind closed doors and concluded that December after around 12 weeks.

The Premier League claimed City breached rules requiring the club to provide "accurate financial information that gives a true and fair view of the club's financial position".

City strongly denied all charges and have said their case is supported by a "comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence".

The club won eight trophies in the period covered by the case, including three Premier League titles, three League Cups, one Community Shield and one FA Cup.

The charges cover the mangerial tenures of Roberto Mancini and Manuel Pellegrini, and the first two years under Pep Guardiola, who left the club after 10 seasons at the end of the 2025-26 campaign .

A separate case between City and the Premier League was also heard last year.

In 2024, an independent arbitration panel found against aspects of the league's Associated Party Transaction regulations (APTs) after City launched an arbitration challenge.

A tribunal held in February 2025 found the Premier League's rules governing sponsorship deals from the period between 2021 and 2024 are "void and unenforceable".

City and the Premier League reached a settlement in September 2025 , with the club accepting the APT rules are valid and binding and both parties agreeing to terminate legal proceedings.

The rules were formed by the Premier League to prevent clubs from profiting from commercial deals with companies linked to their owners that are deemed above "fair market value".

• 54x Failure to provide accurate financial information 2009-10 to 2017-18.

• 14x Failure to provide accurate details for player and manager payments from 2009-10 to 2017-18.

• 5x Failure to comply with Uefa's rules including Financial Fair Play (FFP) 2013-14 to 2017-18.

• 7x Breaching Premier League's Profitability and Sustainability Rules (PSR) 2015-16 to 2017-18.

• 35x Failure to co-operate with Premier League investigations December 2018 - Feb 2023.

There have been suggestions by the Times and football finance expert Kieran Maguire the number of charges is as high as 130. BBC Sport has been unable to verify this.

articles.title: Senegal 'se la pega' en su camino hacia la 'reconquista' de la Copa África
articles.standfirst: Mozambique igualó en el descuento de la primera parte el tanto de Nico Jackson
articles.summary: Mozambique igualó en el descuento de la primera parte el tanto de Nico Jackson
articles.body: La Copa África que los despachos le arrebataron a Senegal para entregársela a Marruecos sigue 'levantando ampollas'. Mientras tanto, los 'Leones de la Teranga' arrancaron la 'reconquista' cediendo un empate contra contra Mozambique (1-1) a domicilio en la primera jornada de los clasificatorios a la próxima CAN. Se estrenaba Patrick Vieira en el banquillo de Senegal... y lo hizo tratando de dejar su sello desde la presentación del once. Ya sin Mendy o Mané, dejó a Koulibaly en el banquillo. Diouf fue quien se enfundó los guantes y Abdallah Sima se ubicó como extremo izquierdo. Pape Gueye partió de inicio en la sala de máquinas junto a Lamine Camara. La avalancha por parte de Senegal arrancó desde primera hora y, nada más superarse la hora de partido, Nico Jackson fue el encargado de abrir el marcador conectando un servicio del propio Sima desde el costado izquierdo. Le valió para reivindicarse al nuevo delantero del Aston Villa tras una Copa del Mundo en la que, incluso, llegó a perder el puesto. El 0-2 parecía mucho más cerca en todo momento. Se durmieron, sin embargo, cuando la primera parte ya había entrado en el tiempo de descuento... y encajaron el empate en el primer remate a puerta de Mozambique en toda la primera parte. Quembo jugó en corto, Geny Catamo recibió en el 'piquito' del área y se sacó un remate que acabó colándose entre un mar de piernas. Vieira, pasada la hora de partido, trató de dotar a Senegal de más vértigo dando entrada a Mbaye por Pape Sarr. Sin embargo, no terminaron de generar un volumen notable de ocasiones como para desnivelar la balanza. Mozambique protegió el marcador y logró sacar un meritorio empate.

articles.title: Celtic & Rangers appeal against Scottish Cup closed doors sanctions
articles.summary: Celtic and Rangers appeal against the Scottish FA decision forcing both clubs to play their next home Scottish Cup ties behind closed doors.
articles.body:
Celtic and Rangers have appealed against the Scottish FA decision that has forced both clubs to play their next home Scottish Cup ties behind closed doors.

The Glasgow clubs are also challenging fines of £100,000 levelled on both after their fans clashed on the pitch at the end of last season's quarter-final at Ibrox, when Celtic progressed after a penalty shoot-out.

Appeal hearings have been set for Monday, 26 October by the governing body.

Both clubs were warned that they could be forced play a second home match without supporters in the event of further unacceptable conduct.

From shaky start to statement wins - 100 days of McInnes at Rangers

Aberdeen lose 500 semi-final tickets after pitch invasion

Scottish Premiership crowds break four million mark

Neither club has commented on their appeals, but Celtic said at the time of the sanctions: "We are shocked by this disproportionate punishment for a relatively small incursion by Celtic supporters at a moment of emotion and celebration.

"Our club has never defended supporters entering the field of play and we have repeatedly taken action when it occurs.

"However, we understand the part emotion plays in football and would have expected the context and distinction in behaviours to have been taken into account by the panel.

"Another important distinction is that, on this occasion, Celtic were not the home club, responsible for stadium safety arrangements."

Both clubs had admitted to the original SFA charges and Rangers said they would consider the outcome in full before determining their response.

Police Scotland have made 43 arrests after fans clashed and officers and stewards were injured following the final whistle in March.

Objects and pyrotechnics were also thrown, with an independent review commissioned by the Scottish FA finding that a "crushing incident was a real and foreseeable risk" due to "non-compliant Ultra group fans surging past police and stewards".

An agreement was reached earlier this month to have no away fans at any of the Old Firm derbies in this season's SPFL competitions.

articles.title: Javi Calleja desvela que el Eldense cuenta ya... con un nuevo presidente
articles.standfirst: El entrenador del club propiedad de Messi lo ha confirmado antes de visitar al Burgos
articles.summary: El entrenador del club propiedad de Messi lo ha asegurado ante los medios
articles.body: Javier Calleja, entrenador del Eldense, desveló este viernes que el club, que pasará a ser propiedad de Lionel Messi, cuenta ya con "un presidente" del que no desveló el nombre pero dijo que les pone "al día de todo lo que sucede" en una entidad que espera a que el CSD autorice la operación de compraventa de las acciones para su anuncio oficial. Entre risas por no poder desvelar la identidad del presidente, el técnico azulgrana apuntó en rueda de prensa que imagina "que en los próximos días se sabrá que hay un presidente". "Con nosotros hay contacto permanente y nos ponen al día de todo lo que está sucediendo", añadió. Javier Calleja aseguró que desde que llegó "se están cumpliendo las expectativas totalmente". "Poco a poco irán saliendo cosas del proyecto que hay, pero el compromiso y la sinceridad con la que me trasladan todo resulta evidente desde el primer día. Hay predisposición absoluta con cada detalle que pedimos para mejorar y trabajar mejor", destacó. Respecto al embargo de un 15% de las acciones de la SAD por una cuestión de los dos anteriores presidentes del Eldense, Calleja señaló: "Desde el club nos transmiten tranquilidad porque esto no tiene nada que ver con la propiedad. Estamos muy tranquilos". En lo deportivo, el entrenador del Eldense manifestó: "Estoy muy contento porque veo que el trabajo diario refuerza que podemos imponer nuestra identidad en cualquier campo para llevar los partidos dónde queremos". "Con el tiempo se verá un equipo más en consonancia con lo que queremos", agregó. Sobre el Burgos, su próximo rival, el entrenador madrileño afirmó que espera "un equipo muy competitivo, compacto, con experiencia y pegada arriba". "Con pocas ocasiones te pueden hacer goles" y "será muy importante no conceder ocasiones para tener opciones de ganar", subrayó. Por último, Javier Calleja confirmó que David Ruiz será baja al menos seis semanas por una rotura muscular y anunció la reincorporación de otros jugadores como Jordi Martín o Javi Olaizola.

articles.title: Sir David Beckham nets £38.5m after World Cup ad deals
articles.summary: His stake in DRJB Holdings has entitled him to almost half of its £85.5m in dividend payments.
articles.body:
Sir David Beckham has netted a £38.5m payout from his sports, fashion, and media business after the 2026 Men's Football World Cup helped it bring in record profits.

The former England star's DRJB Holdings, which includes the Beckham brand, reported an almost £50m profit in 2025, a 46% jump compared to a year earlier. Sales rose from £72.2m to £84m.

The rise was driven by a slew of advertising partnerships struck in the runup to the tournament, including with Bank of America, McDonald's, Verizon, and PepsiCo Lay's.

Sir David, Britain's first billionaire sportsman , was commonly seen in adverts during the summer's World Cup.

In the US, it was difficult for fans to watch a game without coming across Beckham in adverts for Stella Artois, Home Depot and Lay's crisps - known as Walkers in the UK.

Sir David also launched menswear collections for Hugo Boss last year, as well as a pair of Adidas Predator football boots and an eyewear range with Italian glasses maker Safilo.

Revenues at DRJB, of which Beckham owns almost half, were boosted by growth in Beckham's health supplements business too.

DRJB paid its shareholders £38.9m, followed by a special £46.6m payment after the end of the financial year.

Sir David's share of those dividends would have been around £38.5m due to how much of the company he owns.

The remainder of DRJB is owned by New York-based Authentic Brands Group, which also owns Reebok, as well as the rights to other celebrity brands such as comedian and actor Kevin Hart.

Authentic's entertainment chief executive Corey Salter said the performance showed Sir David's name is "one of the most powerful global brands in sport, lifestyle, entertainment and much more".

"It's been an outstanding year, from new partnerships to important philanthropic campaigns and overall brand growth," he said.

Sir David previously drew criticism for associating himself with a country where same-sex relationships are illegal by acting as an ambassador for the 2022 Men's Football World Cup in Qatar.

"It was an important competition and one I was proud to be part of," he said at the time, adding that he had engaged with the LGBTQ community during the tournament.

articles.title: Graham Alexander: Preston North End closing in on appointment of Bradford boss
articles.summary: Preston North End are closing in on the appointment of Bradford City boss Graham Alexander, reports BBC Radio Leeds.
articles.body:
Preston North End are closing in on the appointment of Bradford City boss Graham Alexander, BBC Radio Leeds understands.

Bradford released a statement on Thursday to confirm they had "reluctantly" given the 54-year-old permission to speak to the struggling Championship side.

North End are second bottom and sacked boss Paul Heckingbottom earlier this month after losing six of their first seven league games.

Alexander made 372 league appearances across two spells with the Deepdale side as a player.

Take Me Home EP 60: Emergency pod - Graham Alexander

He has led the Bantams to the top of League One with five wins from their first seven games of the season.

The former Scotland international took over at Valley Parade in November 2023 and won promotion from League Two in his first full season in charge.

They finished fourth in League One in 2025-26 before losing to Bolton Wanderers in the play-offs.

Alexander, who has also had spells in charge of Fleetwood, Scunthorpe, Salford, Motherwell and MK Dons, is contracted to the club until the end of next season.

Preston host Millwall in their first game after the international break on Saturday, 10 October.

Bradford's next League One fixture is on 3 October at Reading with their game this weekend against Barnsley postponed because of international call-ups.

articles.standfirst: El delantero ya fue multado por los tribunales por "falsificación de documentos" y pidió disculpas
articles.summary: El delantero ya fue multado por los tribunales por "falsificación de documentos" y pidió disculpas
articles.body: El delantero de la selección suiza Breel Embolo no estará en los cuatro partidos de Liga de Naciones que el equipo disputa los próximos días, ya que ha sido apartado temporalmente, anunció este viernes la federación helvética pocos días después de que el capitán Granit Xhaka sufriera una medida similar. Aunque la Asociación Suiza de Fútbol (ASF) no precisó en el caso de Embolo las razones de la decisión, la televisión nacional RTS indicó que son las mismas por las que se apartó a Xhaka, ya que ambos falsificaron durante la pandemia certificados de vacunación contra la covid-19. Mientras Xhaka, que en su día reconoció haber sentido desconfianza por las vacunas anticovid, está siendo investigado al respecto por la Fiscalía de Lucerna, Embolo ya fue multado por los tribunales por "falsificación de documentos" y pidió disculpas. El delantero de origen camerunés y actual jugador del Atlanta United, de 29 años, es uno de los máximos goleadores históricos de la Nati, con 26 tantos en 92 internacionalidades. Suiza, que el pasado año bajó de la primera a la segunda categoría de la Liga de Naciones, se estrena en la nueva temporada de la competición fuera de casa contra Macedonia del Norte este sábado, 26 de septiembre, para jugar luego también a domicilio contra Escocia el día 29. Los días 3 y 6 de octubre recibirá en la ciudad suiza de Lucerna primero a eslovenos y a continuación a macedonios.

articles.title: MADCUP consolida su impacto en la Comunidad de Madrid con 89 millones de euros
articles.standfirst: El proyecto da un nuevo paso hacia 2030 con MADCUP WORLD CUP
articles.summary: El proyecto da un nuevo paso hacia 2030 con MADCUP WORLD CUP
articles.body: MADCUP tiene ya un nuevo objetivo en el horizonte: 2030. El proyecto da un nuevo paso en su crecimiento con el lanzamiento de MADCUP WORLD CUP, una iniciativa internacional que reunirá a jóvenes seleccionados de hasta 40 países, que participarán representando a sus respectivos países. Un proyecto que inicia ahora su recorrido hacia 2030, año en el que coincidirán la celebración del Mundial de fútbol en España y el décimo aniversario de MADCUP, y que busca reforzar la dimensión internacional del proyecto y conectar el talento del fútbol base con el ecosistema profesional y la industria del fútbol. Este nuevo proyecto se incorpora a un universo MADCUP que ya tiene nombre propio en la Comunidad de Madrid: 89 millones de euros de impacto económico, según los datos recogidos en su informe de 2026. Una cifra que refleja la dimensión alcanzada por un modelo que articula deporte, educación e industria y que atrae cada año a miles de deportistas, equipos, empresas y profesionales nacionales e internacionales. En el ámbito deportivo, MADCUP FOOTBALL ha reunido en seis ediciones a más de 4.000 equipos de 70 países, mientras que la expansión a nuevas disciplinas continúa consolidándose: MADCUP BASKET alcanzó en su tercera edición los 170 equipos y 1.800 participantes; MADCUP VOLLEY, en su segunda edición, reunió a 112 equipos y más de 1.600 participantes; y MADCUP TENNIS, en su estreno, contó con 24 equipos de cinco países y 540 partidos. A esta dimensión deportiva se suma la apuesta educativa de STEM RACING SPAIN, que en 2026 ha contado con más de 150 equipos y que tendrá a cinco equipos españoles a las finales mundiales de Singapur, así como la dimensión profesional de SPORTS SUMMIT MADRID, punto de encuentro anual y global de la industria deportiva, impulsado por MADCUP, que en su segunda edición superó las 19.000 visitas, con más de 350 marcas representadas y 200 ponentes nacionales e internacionales. Con MADCUP WORLD CUP, MADCUP abre así una nueva etapa en la que el deporte base, el talento joven, la formación y la industria se unen en un mismo camino hacia 2030, reforzando la posición de la Comunidad de Madrid como punto de encuentro internacional para el deporte. El acto fue presentado por Javier Callejo, director de Deportes de Telemadrid, y contó con la presencia de Mariano de Paco Serrano, consejero de Cultura, Turismo y Deporte de la Comunidad de Madrid; Enrique Cerezo, presidente del Atlético de Madrid; Pepe Ortiz, director General de MADCUP; María Benzal, directora Comercial y de Relaciones Internacionales de MADCUP; además de instituciones y empresas que apoyan los proyectos como RFEF, RFFM, IFEMA, Onu Turismo, CEOE, CEIM, ADESP, UFEDEMA, RACE, NEINVER, FNEID o el REAL MADRID.

articles.title: Former Liverpool and England striker Andy Carroll, 37, reveals he was sexually assaulted in 2021 in new autobiography
articles.summary: In his new autobiography, former England footballer Andy Carroll uncovers the traumatic experience of being sexually assaulted in 2021, highlighting its impact on his life and career. Discover the revelations from Carroll's book and his journey towards healing.
articles.body: Former England striker Andy Carroll has revealed that he was sexually assaulted by a man at his home in 2021, an experience he has now described publicly for the first time in his autobiography. Carroll, who was automatically granted anonymity as a victim of sexual assault, said the incident continued to affect his life and his football long after the offender was convicted and jailed.Carroll says the assault happened while he was sleeping at homeCarroll, now 37, revealed the details in his autobiography Owning It, explaining that the assault happened during his second spell with hometown club Newcastle.According to Carroll's account, a friend of his former partner, who was away at the time, had come to his home to watch a boxing match and was staying there. Carroll said the assault happened while he was sleeping.He said he threw the man out of his house after the incident, before knocking him unconscious when the attacker attempted to get back inside.Carroll then called the police and said he was left "sobbing" in the arms of his children's nanny.The offender was subsequently found guilty of sexual offences, sentenced to three years in prison and placed on the sex offender register, with Carroll testifying during the court proceedings.Carroll described giving evidence as "humiliating and embarrassing and absolutely horrendous", while explaining that he had initially been reluctant to make the experience public."I was sexually assaulted, there I said it. Scary to even think about and only a few people knew about it before now," Carroll wrote.He said he decided to include the incident in his book "at the very last minute" after discussing the decision with his girlfriend, Lou Teasdale."Me and Lou spent a lot of time discussing whether to mention it in this book or not. I avoided my publisher for so long that they probably suspected I got cold feet."Carroll said he ultimately decided to tell his story because of the possibility that speaking about what happened could help someone else."Scary to talk about but it's made [me] the person I am today as much as any of the good stuff. And if me talking about it helps just one person then good, it will have been worth it."Carroll says the trauma affected his life and footballCarroll told Owning It that the consequences of the assault extended well beyond the immediate aftermath and affected his ability to concentrate on football."What happened to me affected every facet of my life," he wrote. "I'd think about it every day, making it difficult to focus on anything else, including football ... The trauma of what happened to me hasn't gone away."BBC Sport, reporting on Carroll's account, said the former striker had decided to make the details public in his autobiography after discussing them with Teasdale.Carroll began his career at boyhood club Newcastle United, scoring 31 goals in 80 league appearances in the Premier League and Championship before earning a big-money move to Liverpool in 2011. He later joined West Ham before returning to Newcastle in 2019.The striker subsequently had spells with Reading, West Bromwich Albion and French clubs Amiens and Bordeaux, before joining Dagenham & Redbridge in July 2025 as both a player and co-owner of the National League South club.Carroll represented England nine times between 2010 and 2012. articles.body:
Última hora del Turquía - Francia en directo

Seguimos con la primera jornada de la UEFA Nations League con un gran partido entre Turquía y Francia . Y no es un día cualquiera, porque debuta nada más y nada menos que Zinedine Zidane como técnico galo. Tras cinco años alejado de los banquillos, desde que abandonó el Real Madrid, vuelve a escena para cumplir uno de sus grandes sueños. Ambas selecciones abren su participación en el Grupo A1 de la Liga A , una zona de máxima exigencia que completan Italia y Bélgica .

Les Bleus llegan al partido tras terminar cuartos en el Mundial . Después de 14 años dirigidos por Didier Deschamps , comienza una nueva era en la selección francesa, que busca mantener el nivel de éxito de los últimos años. La primera parada será la Nations League, un torneo que ya conquistaron en 2021. Con un equipo repleto de talento, con Mbappé, Dembélé, Olise y compañía como principales referentes, afrontarán el duelo ante los otomanos con el objetivo de comenzar esta nueva etapa con una victoria.

La selección turca, por su parte, llega después de ser una de las decepciones del Mundial . En un grupo relativamente accesible, no fue capaz de alcanzar los octavos de final. Pese a ello, la federación mantiene su confianza en Vincenzo Montella y en un grupo que debe dar un paso adelante. Arda Güler, convertido en el gran líder de esta generación, será una de las principales amenazas para una Francia que inicia una nueva etapa.

articles.title: India impress against Panama in 1-1 draw as Blue Tigers stand firm against World Cup side
articles.summary: India's national football team held World Cup squad Panama to a 1-1 draw, showcasing their determination with a first-half lead before succumbing to a long-range equalizer, setting the stage for future challenges against Brazil and Uruguay.
articles.body: India had to surrender a first-half lead, but the Blue Tigers came away from Bengaluru with plenty to take from a 1-1 draw against Panama, a side ranked 94 places above them in the FIFA rankings and featuring several players from the country’s recent World Cup campaign. Ryan Williams put India ahead shortly before half-time, only for Omar Valencia to level with a long-range strike in the second half, leaving Khalid Jamil’s side with an encouraging result against the world No. 44 team.Williams rewards India's positive first halfPanama enjoyed more possession during the opening stages, but India stayed compact and looked increasingly dangerous when they broke forward, showing little sign of being overawed by opponents who had competed at the FIFA World Cup only a few months earlier.India created their first clear opening in the eighth minute when Akash Mishra’s cut-back found Williams inside the penalty area, although the forward could not get his shot away. Williams went close again 10 minutes later when he dragged an effort narrowly wide, while Ashique Kuruniyan then found the side-netting as India continued to threaten.The pressure finally produced a breakthrough in the 41st minute. Akash sent a long ball forward, Williams timed his run perfectly to get behind the Panama defence and then kept his composure to beat goalkeeper Marcos Reyes, giving India a 1-0 lead four minutes before the interval.It was a significant moment for a team ranked 138th in the world and playing in Bengaluru for the first time since winning the SAFF Championship at the same stadium in 2023.Panama respond, but India withstand the pressurePanama came out with greater urgency after the restart and quickly began testing the Indian defence. Gurpreet Singh Sandhu was equal to the first major threat, producing a save to deny Giovany Herbert five minutes into the second half.The visitors eventually found their equaliser in the 68th minute, when Valencia struck from outside the box to make it 1-1 and give Panama a platform from which to search for a winner.India still had opportunities to reclaim the lead. Ashique sent a low cross into the box in the 79th minute, but Edmund Lalrindika was unable to make proper contact. Two minutes later, Edmund worked his way in from the right and set up Manvir Singh, who attempted to finish with a backheel rather than taking the simpler option and missed the chance.Panama then pushed forward in search of a decisive goal, striking the woodwork and forcing Gurpreet into another important save. Carlos Harvey, one of the visitors’ World Cup players, also tested the Indian goalkeeper, but India managed to survive the late pressure.Manvir came close again late in the match after being played in by substitute Edmund, while Abhishek Singh Tekcham fired off target following a corner as India continued to carry a threat of their own.India now turn to Brazil and UruguayThe 1-1 draw gives Jamil’s team an important result before a far more demanding sequence of friendlies. India will face five-time world champions Brazil in Kolkata on October 3 before meeting two-time world champions Uruguay at the same venue three days later.For India, the significance of Friday’s result lies not simply in avoiding defeat against Panama, but in the way the Blue Tigers competed against a side ranked 44th in the world. Williams’ first-half finish gave them a lead to protect, Panama eventually found a way through, and India still created enough opportunities afterwards to believe they could have taken all three points.The next two fixtures will provide a considerably tougher test, but the performance in Bengaluru has given Jamil’s side something substantial to carry into them.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Sigue la fiesta de España en el Mundial: ¡Héctor Álvarez se lleva la plata!
articles.standfirst: El español vuelve a subir al podio en Montreal tras una carrera desatada en la que Ashlin Barry, nacido en Girona, conquistó el arcoíris con una escapada de más de 120 kilómetros
articles.summary: El español vuelve a subir al podio en Montreal tras una carrera desatada en la que Ashlin Barry conquistó el arcoíris con una escapada de más de 120 kilómetros
articles.body: Héctor Álvarez volvió a demostrar en Montreal que está hecho para las grandes citas. El español conquistó la medalla de plata en el Mundial sub-23 en ruta después de una carrera salvaje, imposible de domesticar, que terminó coronando al estadounidense Ashlin Barry. El nuevo campeón del mundo convirtió una aventura iniciada a más de 120 kilómetros de meta en una hazaña monumental, mientras Álvarez fue el más fuerte entre todos los que intentaron echar abajo su desafío. España llegaba a la prueba con la moral disparada después del festival de Benja Noval en categoría júnior y con Álvarez señalado como una de las grandes bazas para volver a pisar el podio. El circuito de Montreal, con 174 kilómetros y doce pasos por meta, no dejó apenas un minuto para respirar. Desde la salida comenzaron los ataques, se formaron grupos numerosos y la carrera quedó abierta mucho antes de que aparecieran los favoritos. Eñaut Urkaregi fue uno de los españoles más activos en la primera mitad de la jornada, entrando en varios movimientos mientras por delante se sucedían las fugas. La definitiva comenzó a tomar cuerpo a 126 kilómetros de meta, cuando Samuel Novak, William Heffernan, Kristian Egholm, Matthew Dodd y Barry lograron abrir hueco. Lo que entonces parecía otro movimiento más terminó escondiendo al futuro campeón del mundo. El pelotón concedió demasiado. La diferencia superó los dos minutos y, aunque por detrás empezaron a sucederse los ataques, Barry resistió siempre en cabeza. Primero acompañado y después cada vez más cerca de quedarse solo. A 30 kilómetros del final, con Egholm ya descolgado, el estadounidense afrontó en solitario una persecución que parecía condenada a terminar con su captura. Tenía únicamente 29 segundos sobre el pelotón. Ahí apareció Héctor. El español había empezado a enseñar los dientes antes, con un primer ataque a 38 kilómetros de meta que hizo daño y seleccionó muchísimo el grupo. No consiguió marcharse, pero dejó claro que no estaba dispuesto a esperar. Cuando la carrera volvió a romperse, Álvarez entró en cada movimiento importante y asumió buena parte de la responsabilidad de intentar acabar con la resistencia de Barry. A 26 kilómetros del final, Héctor formaba parte de un pequeño grupo perseguidor junto a hombres como Matisse Van Kerckhove, Guus van den Eijnden y Cameron Rogers. Barry estaba apenas a 23 segundos. arecía cazado. Parecía cuestión de tiempo. Pero no lo fue. El estadounidense encontró fuerzas donde ya no parecía haberlas. Matteo Scalco atacó por detrás y posteriormente fue el propio Álvarez quien lanzó otro movimiento a 20 kilómetros de meta, seleccionando definitivamente la pelea por las medallas. El español logró marcharse junto a Scalco, Aubin Sparfel, Jesper Stiansen y Niels Driesen. Barry estaba a solo 26 segundos. Era el momento decisivo. Por detrás había entendimiento, piernas y nombres suficientes para acabar con la escapada. Por delante, sin embargo, Barry rodaba como si la persecución no existiera. La diferencia, lejos de desaparecer, volvió a crecer. Al comienzo de la última vuelta, a 13 kilómetros del final, tenía 42 segundos. El oro empezaba a dejar de ser un sueño para convertirse en una realidad. Álvarez comprendió entonces que el arcoíris se alejaba y tuvo que cambiar de objetivo. Ya no se trataba de cazar al estadounidense, sino de asegurar una medalla en un grupo cargado de corredores rápidos y peligrosos. A diez kilómetros de meta, Barry conservaba 35 segundos. A cinco, la diferencia seguía por encima de los 40. No hubo milagro. Barry entró en meta para completar una de las grandes exhibiciones de este Mundial, culminando una aventura iniciada a 126 kilómetros de la llegada. Detrás, Héctor Álvarez ganó la batalla por la plata y confirmó su condición de gran realidad del ciclismo español. El oro se escapó, pero Montreal volvió a regalar otra medalla a España. Y Álvarez, después de haber buscado la carrera, atacado, seleccionado el grupo y perseguido hasta el límite, terminó subiendo al segundo escalón del podio. Solo un hombre, y una fuga de locos, pudieron con él.

articles.title: MSU football to host Illinois ATH with power four offer this weekend
articles.summary: An intriguing athlete prospect from Illinois is set to visit Michigan State on Saturday for the Spartans' home game against Nebraska
articles.body:
An intriguing athlete prospect from Illinois is set to visit Michigan State on Saturday for the Spartans ' home game against Nebraska .

Javonte Williams of Wheaton, Ill. announced on Friday that he'll be visiting Michigan State this upcoming weekend. According to a social media post from Williams, he will be visiting the Spartans for their home game against the Nebraska Cornhuskers on Saturday.

Williams is listed as an athlete prospect in the 2028 class, and plays for St. Francis High School. He is listed at 5-foot-11 and 165 pounds, according to 247Sports.

Williams is currently unranked and unrated by both 247Sports and Rivals at the time of this post.

Michigan State football has not yet extended an offer to Williams, but he does hold a handful of offers from other FBS schools. According to a pair of recruiting services, Williams has offers from Pittsburgh , Northern Illinois , Miami (OH) and Marshall. Nebraska has also shown interest in him as well.

Williams is one of many prospects that'll be in attendance for the Spartans' home game against Nebraska this weekend. This is a massive recruiting weekend for Michigan State, with players from the 2027, 2028 and 2029 class expected to visit.

articles.summary: Texas football coach Steve Sarkisian shed light on how the president’s presence could affect a game, sparking outrage among some fans.
articles.body:
There may be a reason behind the "Trump curse" — but it's not witchcraft.

At least, according to the University of Texas Longhorns' head football coach Steve Sarkisian , who recently shed light on a challenge coaches face whenever President Donald Trump decides he wants to attend a game.

"The one thing that you have to be aware of when the president goes to any game is that any time he enters the stadium, leaves the stadium or changes locations within the stadium, they cut all communication," Sarkisian told reporters on a Zoom call on Thursday. "So they cut your headsets. They cut the headsets to coaches. They cut headsets for coach-to-player communication. So you have to have a plan for that, if and when it happens, and you get no warning. It just gets cut out."

Sarkisian made his remarks ahead of the throwdown between the Longhorns and Tennessee Volunteers this Saturday in Knoxville's Neyland Stadium — a game Trump is scheduled to attend .

"You have to have a plan to adjust if and when he comes in the middle of the first quarter, leaves in the fourth quarter, or decides he's got to use the restroom, whatever that looks like," Sarkisian continued, talking about having to deal with the president's whims. "You've got to be prepared to have no communication for a short amount of time."

Like this article? Keep independent journalism alive. Support HuffPost .

Later Thursday, in an interview with On Texas Football , Sarkisian elaborated on the issue and provided an example he heard from University of Miami coach Mario Cristobal.

"A good friend of mine is Mario Cristobal," he said, "Last year, when they were playing Indiana in the national championship, they had that drive at the end of that game.

"They had no communication because [Trump] was leaving early before the game ended. And so you get no warning. It just cuts out ... and so you've got to be prepared for that. That is definitely something that is unique that could come up in this ball game."

The idea that Trump may have impacted last season's championship game sent some college football fans into a spiral.

Former Meet the Press host Chuck Todd said om X : "***!!!?!? Are you telling me that Trump cost Miami in the final drive? Is that what Sark is saying? I went into a bit of sports media blackout post-Miami loss in that game, but was this widely reported post-game?"

"You kidding me??" said sports writer Alex Donno in a post on X . "They cut off Miami's comms with no warning during the final drive of the title game down 6???"

"A pretty insane story given the timing and stakes," echoed sports analyst CJ Vogel on X .

The dramatic timing of the cutout in Sarkisian's story has been disputed and downplayed by some involved with both teams.

An anonymous source on Miami's 2025 staff told The Athletic "that the outage occurred before the last drive." Indiana's Curt Cignetti told ESPN that the headsets went out around the 6:45 mark, when Miami had the ball.

"It came back before kickoff," Cignetti told ESPN. "We both had communication from that point on."

CBS Sports also spoke with multiple sources in the Miami program about the communication blip. Two sources told CBS the lapse did not happen on the final drive. All the sources "were adamant" that the cutout only lasted a "couple plays" and didn't "notably impact the outcome of the game."

Despite whether Trump screwed over Miami or not, some sports fans believe that Trump's attendance at sporting events leads to bad luck — especially for the president's favored team.

The phrase "Trump curse" as it pertains to sports popped up on social media after the president allegedly jinxed the New York Knicks in Game 3 of the NBA Finals, and when the United States lost to Belgium in the World Cup — despite Trump trying to goose the game in U.S. favor. Most recently, New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart — who introduced Trump at an event in May — suffered a knee injury Monday night against the Los Angeles Rams that requires surgery and will keep him out for the rest of the regular season.

Many others have extended the "Trump curse" to describe pretty much anything the president touches, like the demolition of the White House East Wing, the botched renovation of the Reflecting Pool , his poorly attended Great American State Fair …or, by extension, the current state of the nation as a whole.

articles.title: The Man City verdict is an earthquake – what comes next could be even bigger
articles.summary: ANALYSIS: With Man City expected to be found guilty of most of the 115 charges, the Premier League has a highly significant first victory in one of the most...
articles.body:
Perhaps the most seismic day in English football history, but one that is still going to see more earthquakes to come – and perhaps for some time.

As news broke from The Athletic that Manchester City are expected to be found guilty of most of the 115 charges – with sources insisting the same to the The Independent – there was still no official Premier League statement. The competition is still subject to a private and confidential process, amid a situation that remains legally sensitive.

While many figures in football found this "absurd" given how reports on this are the talk of the game, after 24 hours of rumours that a decision was imminent, it also points to how – in the words of one source – "this is nowhere near the end".

City are expected to appeal, "trying every route possible", potentially including the High Court, even though that is not strictly permitted in the rules.

And that already in a situation where, without an actual published award, the entire case still forms one of the longest waits for a civil award in English modern legal history.

It all means that, despite a huge step after eight years of waiting , there is still so much uncertainty.

Many involved do seem to have been caught cold by the news. Everyday City staff were not forewarned, which marks a difference from previous steps in this eight-year process, and many were resorting to gallows humour once the news came out.

While there was a lot of "chatter" that something was about to come out after Thursday's Premier League meeting, no one knew the fine details.

Outside City, responses have ranged from relief to shock. There is genuine surprise that the Premier League are expected to win so many of the charges, mostly due to the risk of having more than 100 of them and "the legal firepower being deployed".

Some sources were describing City as "internally measured", with the general statement to media reflecting that : that they were still insisting on innocence.

"The Premier League process remains ongoing, with significant elements to be completed, and subject to strict confidentiality. As such Manchester City 's position remains consistent with the club's statement of February 2023."

Many within the Premier League were also struck by the tone of the second paragraph.

"The club has diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis that the Premier League board and executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair-minded regulator, free from partisan influence."

Around the same time as the story first broke, new City coach Enzo Maresca put up a social media post with the caption: "Time to breathe. Time to analyse. Time to learn."

The photos included feet on grass, a swimming pool and a quote attributed to Socrates saying: "The only thing I know is that I know nothing."

We do now, for the first time since the charges were announced in February 2023 , know something .

The fact the whole process is still ongoing, however, leaves the situation with many ifs and question marks despite this first full-stop.

Or, as one executive said, "this story has more chapters in it".

Many of the questions are the same as before, albeit now with the clarity of an expected outcome, and – crucially – the presence of the Independent Football Regulator.

That body does have powers under section 34.

If City are indeed found guilty of the most serious charges, the regulator could push for the removal of key figures.

Some in football are even broaching the idea of a forced sale due to the severity of the case, given that this would be perceived as the greatest case of cheating in English football history.

It should not be forgotten that this is ultimately about the allegation of submitting false accounting.

The charges didn't just involve accusations of breaching financial regulations on several occasions, but of not providing accurate payment details.

A sanctions hearing would determine the most immediate punishments. Multiple sources feel this can't possibly go without a huge points deduction, particularly given the recent precedent of Everton and Nottingham Forest , potentially enough to relegate the club.

Many feel such a quantity of guilty verdicts would nevertheless be sufficient grounds for outright expulsion from the league .

But what happens if the appeal goes on? What if City win the league this season if any punishments are not applied now? What if punishments are applied and the appeal is successful?

Will aggrieved clubs push for legal compensation, having missed out on league titles and Champions League places?

And then there are all the other sub-plots and threads. Pep Guardiola's departure now looks impeccably timed . He doesn't have to answer questions on any of this.

Rodri and Erling Haaland may have to, though.

City's former captain was due to speak to media in London, of all places, ahead of Spain's Nations League fixture against England.

Haaland has similar duties planned for Saturday.

There are just so many implications all round. Could players have grounds for termination?

Other executives see City's statement as "very punchy", that potentially turns this cold war into a civil war.

Within that, though, amid so much criticism of the process and even their governance, the Premier League has a highly significant first victory.

Pep Guardiola left Man City in the summer after saying he believed the club did not break Premier League rules (PA)
Enzo Maresca has since taken charge at the Etihad and has led the club to five straight Premier League wins (PA)
Man City are expected to appeal the verdict, in a saga that could yet drag on for even longer (Getty)

articles.title: Stanford strikes deal with DoorDash for jersey-patch sponsorship
articles.summary: Stanford announced a multiyear sponsorship agreement with DoorDash on Friday, in the latest example of college athletic departments trying to tap into fresh...
articles.body:
Another day, another college sports sponsorship agreement.

Stanford announced a multiyear partnership with DoorDash on Friday. The agreement includes a jersey patch on Cardinal uniforms in at least 15 varsity programs, according to the school's news release, and marks the largest sponsorship deal in the history of Stanford's athletic department.

Cardinal football players will wear the jersey patch starting with Saturday night's home game against Georgia Tech.

The deal with DoorDash also is notable because its co-founders are Stanford alums Tony Xu, Andy Fang and Stanley Tang. They and classmate Evan Moore (who has since left the company) launched DoorDash, first known as Palo Alto Delivery, as a class project in 2013. The company now has its headquarters in San Francisco.

One day earlier, on Thursday, Cal announced a sponsorship agreement with Databricks, a data and AI company also based in San Francisco. That deal covers naming rights to the field at Memorial Stadium and a helmet logo; the company's founders similarly are alums of the school.

These alliances reflect the changing landscape of college sports , with revenue sharing, NIL deals and conference realignment (namely, rising travel costs) putting massive financial pressure on athletic departments. Cal and Stanford are both increasingly trying to tap into the Bay Area's corporate community, especially in technology - where their graduates have made a widespread impact.

Among the Stanford teams beyond football set to feature DoorDash apparel: men's and women's basketball, men's and women's soccer, baseball, softball and women's volleyball. The company also will have a "prominent presence across multiple department venues," according to Friday's news release, in signage and digital display.

"DoorDash is one of the world's most iconic brands and an innovative industry pioneer whose origin is synonymous to our university," Stanford athletic director John Donahoe said in a statement. "The same ingenuity, hustle and perseverance that defined the company's humble beginnings are trademark characteristics embodied by our student-athletes on the field and in the classroom."

Cardinal teams also will incorporate their new sponsor into meal planning for athletes and staff members.

Xu, the company's CEO, said in the news release, "DoorDash is proud to support the school where our journey began as a class project 13 years ago. It's humbling to team up with Stanford Athletics and its student-athletes to celebrate and encourage their drive, commitment and ambition to do big things."

articles.title: Five Bold Predictions For Ohio State vs. Illinois
articles.summary: We haven't hit on many over our bold predictions, but Ohio State vs. Illinois gives us another opportunity! Who steps up this week?
articles.body:
Bold predictions are a fun way to keep attention on a game that could otherwise be incredibly boring. For some, actually betting on random props helps them. For us, let's just stick to writing about them here for Last Word. Last week, we weren't able to get the bold predictions for Ohio State vs. Kent State out due to how hectic life has been (full-time stay-at-home dad to a two-year-old, renovating a house, managing Last Word on NFL , calling five high school soccer games in four days for radio, etc., etc., etc.), but we did utilize the old Tweet machine .

As a result, we finally got one right. Our season total looks a lot like this author's batting stats in his senior year of high school. But we keep chugging on!

Five Bold Predictions For Ohio State vs. Illinois

With how the Ohio State offensive line has played through the first three games – fine; not horrible, but not elite – not allowing a sack in any game would certainly qualify as a bold prediction. Against Ball State, Julian Sayin was sacked twice. Against Texas, he was sacked twice. Last week, that number was just one sack, but five sacks through three games (two of which against two of the worst MAC programs) is not ideal.

As of the Thursday evening availability report, starting right tackle Phillip Daniels is still questionable to appear in this matchup. As a result, the Buckeyes will likely go with Austin Siereveld at right tackle again, with Gabe VanSickle at right guard.

Last year, the Illini pass rush was one guy. That one guy is in the NFL. In Illinois's three games, it has recorded just three sacks, with one coming in each game. Only amassing one sack against Duke is what it is; only getting one sack against Southern Illinois (FCS) should be concerning for the Illini.

In the matchup last season, Sayin was not sacked on 27 pass attempts.

The ground game in Columbus has fallen short of expectations to this point. Bo Jackson leads the rushing attack with 230 yards and two touchdowns on 39 attempts. Oddly enough, Ja'Kobi Jackson has taken over that goal-line sniper role and leads the team with four touchdowns. Of course, he also leads the room with 7.1 yards per carry.

Jackson has not gone over 100 yards yet this year. This is mostly due to the fact that he has only one run for 18 yards or more. Against Ball State, he took off for a 65-yard touchdown. Against Texas, his longest run was 11 yards. Last week, that long was just 17 yards.

Naturally, the fanbase has been nostalgic for the times of TreVeyon Henderson , J.K. Dobbins, and Ezekiel Elliott , who could score from anywhere on the field. At the same time, the Fringe™ has been clamoring for Legend Bey (who has two snaps over the last two games).

Jackson still doesn't have that track star speed, but he was able to make it work with his vision and ability to make guys miss. That hasn't been the case as much this year. He needs a big game at some point, so why not this week?

3. Another Interception From A Linebacker

Over the first two weeks, we predicted Jay Timmons would get an interception. We went oh-for-two. However, in the wake of that, two linebackers secured interceptions. TJ Alford made the play in Week 1, while Riley Pettijohn came down with an interception last week.

This week, it'll be more of the same. Katin Houser is going to have to throw the ball, both because Ohio State should be in control of the game and because the Buckeyes' run defense has been quite good. As a result, there will be plenty of opportunities for Alford, Pettijohn, Payton Pierce , and Christian Alliegro .

At the same time, Devin Sanchez has another solid test this week in the form of Collin Dixon. The Illini leading receiver leads the nation with seven receiving touchdowns, so the script will focus on him. If Sanchez is able to step up, that means Houser will have to check down and look in the middle of the field for his second and third options. That opens things up for the linebackers.

This prediction is bold on a number of fronts. First, Qua Russaw hasn't done anything with the Buckeyes just yet. Second, Ohio State has only forced two fumbles, and neither was a fumble by the quarterback. Third, the Buckeye defense has only recorded four sacks (two from the defensive line). Why not try to buck all of those trends?

Russaw was a big name the Buckeyes nabbed in the transfer portal. At Alabama, Russaw saw a moderate amount of time, and transferred to Ohio State with two sacks under his belt. He was held out of the Week 1 win, but over the last two weeks, he's earned 59 snaps. With those 59 snaps, Russaw has managed three tackles and one tackle for loss. That's not exactly the level of contributions the Buckeyes are looking for at that position.

We've mentioned this before, but the defensive end/EDGE group needs someone to step up. Gone are the days of Chase Young , Nick Bosa , and Joey Bosa . Kenyatta Jackson Jr. is the leader of the group, with his one sack thus far, and Epi Sitanilei has the other. That's it.

Russaw is a solid player, and he may not have been 100% against Texas and/or Kent State. Against Illinois, he has a great opportunity to make an impact.

5. Connor Hawkin Hits a 50+ Yard Field Goal

The Illinois defense isn't the best that Ohio State will face, but it's not awful. The Illini will likely get a stop or two on the day. Now, whether that is due to them making the play or because Ohio State can't get out of its own way on third or fourth down is another question. However, that means if a drive stalls, Ryan Day will turn to his kicker to get some points.

Last year, Ohio State attempted two field goals and made both (41 yards and 26 yards). Of course, one of the drives that ended in a punt stalled at the Illinois 41-yard line. Jayden Fielding didn't have that kind of leg; Connor Hawkins does. He could make a 56-yard field goal if asked.

Last year, as a member of the Baylor Bears' program, Hawkins hit three of his four 50+ yard attempts. His long on the year was from 54, so trying to hit a 56-yarder would be a stretch.

Either way, unless the Buckeyes are able to fix those third-down issues, Hawkins should have a couple of opportunities to make an impact. Maybe it'll get the Ohio State fans off his back after missing one of his four kicks against Texas.

Where : Ohio Stadium, Columbus, Ohio History : Ohio State 69-30-4 Illinois (2010 win vacated) Last Matchup : Ohio State won, 34-16, in 2025 Last Illinois Win: 28-21 in 2007 Date and Time : 12:00 p.m. ET How to Watch : FOX Spread : Ohio State -27.5; O/U 54.5 (via FanDuel)

Prediction : Kicking off the Big Ten slate with a bang has to be on the minds of Ryan Day and the Buckeyes. A four-touchdown spread is impressive, but Ohio State is 3-0 ATS at this point (barely). Vegas knows what the Buckeyes are. Let's go with Ohio State winning this one and retaining the famed Illibuck, 45-10.
